s1.description: Opening: where this session sits, what students will be able to do, and the 3-hour plan

s2.description: Block 1: FEM as a PDE solver, scalar versus vector fields, where civil engineers meet heat conduction

s3.description: Block 2: derivation of the steady heat conduction PDE from an energy balance and Fourier’s law, and its matrix form

s4.description: Block 3: Dirichlet and Neumann conditions, the rectangular-domain simplification, and what each type means for FEM

s5.description: Block 4: degrees of freedom and derivation of the bilinear shape functions of the four-node rectangular element, with their properties

s6.description: Block 5: derivatives of the shape functions, the gradient and flux inside an element, and a one-slide preview of the eight-node element

s7.description: Block 6: the seven-step FEM pipeline, the MATLAB skeleton that follows it, exit ticket and preparation for Heat Transfer Part 2
